title: How are the rows and columns of twelve figs related to twelve?
description: {{NAME_1}} lists the rectangles that twelve figs can make, and the board compares the rows and columns of each one with twelve. Keeko doubts the link and says that rows plus columns make twelve.
teaching_notes: One idea: in a rectangle of figs, the number of rows times the number of columns gives the number of figs, so the rows and the columns are factors of that number. Watch for students who add the rows and the columns instead of multiplying them.

source: Observe the number of rows and columns in each of the arrang
video_script.why: The child reads the rows and columns of each rectangle of twelve figs and sees that their product is always twelve, which makes each of them a factor of twelve.
video_script.substitution: Multiply the rows by the columns for each rectangle and compare with twelve.
video_script.anchor: The rectangles of twelve figs that {{NAME_1}} has listed, shown in rows and columns
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko adds the rows and the columns. Two rows of six figs give two plus six, which is eight, and not twelve, while two times six gives twelve, so the doubt is crossed out.
video_script.payoff_line: Rows times columns gives twelve, so the rows and the columns are factors of twelve.

final_answer.value: rows × columns = 12, so the number of rows or columns are factors of 12
final_answer.spoken: rows times columns gives twelve, so each of them is a factor

names.{{NAME_1}}: lists the rectangles that twelve figs can make

maths_rules: the rectangles of 12 figs: 1 row of 12, 2 rows of 6, 3 rows of 4
each of 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12 divides 12 exactly, so each is a factor of 12
video_script.design: Three rectangles of twelve figs with their rows and columns written beside them in a table; the product column fills with twelve each time.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; a box of twelve figs; three rectangles of figs listed by the child; the words rows and columns

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about the figs.
<bookmark mark='list'/>{{NAME_1}} has listed the rectangles that twelve figs can make.
<bookmark mark='look'/>Look at the rows and the columns of each rectangle. How are they related to twelve?

beats.on_screen: the three rectangles stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a rectangle of figs with its rows drawn across and its columns drawn down; every row holds the same number of figs

marks.rows: the rows are drawn across in teal
marks.cols: the columns are drawn down in amber
marks.same: the figs in each row are counted

narration: <bookmark mark='rows'/>Rows run across the rectangle, and columns run down it.
<bookmark mark='cols'/>Two rows of six figs have two rows and six columns.
<bookmark mark='same'/>Every row has the same number of figs, so counting the figs row by row is multiplying.

beats.on_screen: Given: 3 rectangles of 12 figs: 1 row of 12, 2 rows of 6, 3 rows of 4

marks.given: the three rectangles are written as rows and columns

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, three rectangles of twelve figs. They have one row of twelve, two rows of six and three rows of four.

beats.on_screen: To find: how rows and columns are related to 12

marks.find: the words to find are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find how the rows and the columns are related to twelve.

beats.on_screen: a table: rows 1, 2, 3; columns 12, 6, 4; rows × columns 12, 12, 12

marks.table: the table of rows and columns is drawn
marks.mult: the rows and columns of each line are multiplied

narration: <bookmark mark='table'/>Step one, write the rows and the columns of each rectangle in a table.
<bookmark mark='mult'/>Multiply the rows by the columns. One times twelve, two times six and three times four are each twelve.
<bookmark mark='same'/>The answer is twelve every time.

marks.each: the numbers in the table are circled
marks.divide: twelve is shared equally by each circled number
marks.check: a check with six rows of two figs is drawn

narration: <bookmark mark='each'/>Step two, look at the numbers of rows and columns. They are one, two, three, four, six and twelve.
<bookmark mark='divide'/>Each of them divides twelve exactly, because it multiplies with another number to make twelve.
<bookmark mark='check'/>Check with six rows of two figs. Six times two is twelve, so that fits as well.

beats.on_screen: Answer: rows × columns = 12, so the rows and the columns are factors of 12
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Rows times columns gives twelve, so the rows and the columns are factors of twelve.
<bookmark mark='name'/>That is how the arrangements are related to twelve.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the answer
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's doubt: rows + columns = 12, crossed out; 2 + 6 = 8 against 2 × 6 = 12

marks.doubt: Keeko's doubt appears in a bubble
marks.add: the rows and the columns of the second rectangle are added
marks.mult: the rows and the columns are multiplied beside it

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks rows plus columns make twelve.
<bookmark mark='add'/>Take two rows of six figs. Two plus six is only eight.
<bookmark mark='mult'/>Two times six is twelve, which counts every fig.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>We must multiply the rows by the columns, and adding does not count the figs.
